haiku-low.q1: MySQL transaction changes the user, upserts users_pg_pending, and commits first. Then Postgres is safe-copied with a 500 ms timeout. If Postgres fails, the caller still gets success.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the id is not in that database's users_tombstones and the incoming version is higher than the stored version.
haiku-low.q3: Step 3 must be confirmed on every instance, and at least 1 minute must pass. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s after a flag change.
haiku-low.q4: Backfill waits while replica lag exceeds 5 s. It reads from the MySQL replica in batches of at most 2,000 rows, one Postgres transaction per batch.
haiku-low.q5: Reads move after a clean comparer pass with 0 mismatches. The source of truth moves after reads hold at 100% for 3 days with a clean latest nightly pass.
haiku-low.q6: A pending row in the source-of-truth database, written in the same transaction as the change. The MySQL sweeper repairs Postgres within about 15 s, or once Postgres recovers.
haiku-low.q7: Copies and deletes both take a per-id lock first. Safe copy skips any id in users_tombstones, so a deleted user cannot be re-created.
haiku-low.q8: Progress lives in users_backfill_progress. Each batch's copy and last_copied_id update commit in one Postgres transaction. It stops when no rows at or below target_max_id remain.
haiku-low.q9: The comparer walks both databases in 10,000-id chunks, comparing id, version and hash. It rechecks differences on the primary 5 s later. Persistent ones are queued to pending for the sweeper to repair.
haiku-low.q10: Frozen blocks writes until confirmed plus 5 s, and pending is drained first. If not done by T0+60 s, set dual_mysql_primary instead; writes resume by T0+90 s.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns new ids after step 8, with its identity set to MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT counter. After rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set past Postgres's next value.
haiku-low.q12: Postgres writes are mirrored to MySQL via users_mysql_pending and sweeper repair. Rollback freezes writes, drains pending, sets MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, then restores dual_mysql_primary. The option ends at pg_only in step 10.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first: one MySQL transaction changes the user and upserts users_pg_pending, commits (write succeeded), then the row is safe-copied to Postgres (500 ms timeout). If the Postgres part fails or times out, the caller still sees success; the pending row stays.
sonnet.q2: Only when the incoming version is higher than the existing row's version (and the id is not in Postgres users_tombstones; if absent it is inserted).
sonnet.q3: Step 3 (dual_mysql_primary) must be confirmed on every instance (app_flag_value shows it everywhere) and at least 1 minute must have passed since. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s after a flag change.
sonnet.q4: NOT STATED beyond: it reads from the MySQL replica (not the primary), only while replica lag is 5 s or less (waits if above), in batches of at most 2,000 rows. (It reads the primary only once for max(id).) No other throttling is described.
sonnet.q5: Reads: backfill done and one complete comparer pass with 0 mismatches (step 5). Source of truth: reads at 100% for at least 3 days, with the latest nightly comparer pass showing 0 mismatches; also a quiet time; then the freeze sequence (frozen confirmed +5 s, users_pg_pending empty, Postgres identity restarted at MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT n).
sonnet.q6: A row in users_pg_pending (in MySQL), upserted in the same transaction as the user change so it survives a crash after commit. The MySQL sweeper (every 10 s, rows older than 5 s) re-reads the user from MySQL, safe-copies to Postgres, and deletes the pending row if its token is unchanged.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: every delete removes the row and inserts the id into users_tombstones in the same transaction, in both databases. Safe copy skips any id in that database's tombstones, and copy and delete take a per-id lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock in Postgres; locking read of users_tombstones in MySQL) so they cannot interleave.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres table users_backfill_progress (one row: last_copied_id, target_max_id). Each batch's safe-copy and the update of last_copied_id happen in one Postgres transaction, so they roll back together. It stops when no rows remain at or below target_max_id, the max(id) on the MySQL primary read at start (higher ids are already dual-written).
sonnet.q9: The comparer: walks both databases 10,000 ids at a time comparing id, version and a hash of other columns (MySQL from replica, pausing if lag > 5 s). It re-checks each difference on the source-of-truth primary after 5 s; if still different it is a mismatch, and the id is added to the pending table in the source-of-truth database, where the sweeper repairs it. Each pass reports its mismatch count; runs nightly.
sonnet.q10: Set write_mode = frozen (instances answer writes with retryable 503), wait until confirmed (up to 30 s) plus 5 s write deadline, so no old-mode write can commit; then empty pending, reset the Postgres identity, and set dual_pg_primary (instances resume within 30 s). If sub-steps 2 to 5 are not done by T0 + 60 s, set dual_mysql_primary instead (nothing to undo; retry another day). Last instance resumes writes by T0 + 90 s either way.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids (identity column). Before switching, it is restarted with ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN id RESTART WITH n, where n is MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT counter (above every id MySQL issued, including tombstoned ones). For rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set to the Postgres identity's next value so MySQL cannot reissue an id Postgres used; also inserting an explicit id into MySQL moves AUTO_INCREMENT past it.
sonnet.q12: Each Postgres write upserts users_mysql_pending in the same transaction, then safe-copies to MySQL (500 ms timeout); the Postgres sweeper repairs failures, and the nightly comparer treats Postgres as truth. Rollback (any time in step 9, needs Postgres reachable): freeze, confirm +5 s, wait for users_mysql_pending empty, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT to Postgres identity's next value, set dual_mysql_primary and read_from_pg = 0; if not complete by T0 + 60 s, revert to dual_pg_primary; writes resume by T0 + 90 s. The option ends at the first pg_only write (step 10), the point of no return.
